label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.

findings.quote: the designer wrote a third note, and dev built the designer's first
findings.why: Four members and their separate tasks are packed into one sentence, so a first reader cannot tell who did what to whose work.

findings.quote: What the record shows is not whether everything finished, but whether
findings.why: The narrator reports what the record shows with no I and no hindsight, at the very point a newsroom builder wants his judgement.

findings.quote: Like the night's first case, these had gone out with the first push.
findings.why: It leans on a failure from an earlier chapter without a half-line saying what it was, so this chapter stalls for anyone who opened it directly.

findings.quote: A request not picked up at one session is picked up at the next. Nobody chased it.
findings.why: The same 'nobody chased it' idea comes again in the section title at line 109 and in line 123.

findings.quote: answered at the next and used at the one after, with nobody chasing it.
findings.why: This is the third telling of the same point (lines 34 and 109), and the record note itself says it is told once in chapter 10.

findings.quote: A piece marked ready for me, then another. A list of what waits on me, refreshed every hour.
findings.why: A run of clipped sentences ends the section, where one running sentence would carry the queue building up better.

findings.quote: what did not finish said so, and the night's failure, found a third time, is kept.
findings.why: It restates the partial-wake point of line 30 and the third finding of line 48 almost word for word as a close.

findings.quote: the temptation is to start asking straight away.
findings.why: It tells the reader what they will be tempted to do; for me the card is also the only takeaway, and it is two lines against nine hours.

findings.quote: What your own team can take from them is the same at every stop
findings.why: The takeaway is promised once and then never made at any stop, so a builder who wants something to copy gets only descriptions.

findings.quote: The words the agents say are ours, written for this book
findings.why: 'Ours' replaces the narrator's I with a plural that nothing else in the section uses.

findings.quote: The same three circles, drawn in front of the room one by one, so the overlap arrives last.
findings.why: Stop 4 (line 60) has already told the three circles and their overlap, so stop 5 repeats the scene.

findings.quote: The home page says the perfect storm.
findings.why: 'The perfect storm' is used as a known phrase before the section has said what the storm is.

findings.quote: The **check** (the team called it the gate)
findings.why: Chapter 9 says 'gate' and 'post_check' without a gloss, and the gloss here sits in the back matter under a different headword, so a reader looking up 'gate' finds nothing.

findings.quote: The clock in the margin counts the talk's day in **hours**
findings.why: It is the only entry not starting with its headword, so it sits between 'hold' and 'lock' out of order and is easy to miss when scanning.

what_holds: 09-nine-hours-with-nobody-starting-work.md: the partial wake that says it is partial and the morning review's 'what only you can decide' are exactly the editor-who-signs pattern a newsroom builder wants to copy.

09-nine-hours-with-nobody-starting-work.md: the narrator's 'I am not going to skip them, because quiet is the evidence' and the empty bench at hour fourteen give the nine hours a human voice; the failures stay in.
90-the-tour-at-length.md: each stop is short and carries one line from the agent that made the page, so it can be walked quickly.
91-the-words-used.md: plain one-line definitions with a chapter pointer each; 'hold', 'wake' and 'scope' are usable as they stand.
notes: Clean overall; no finding rises to must. For this persona chapter 9 is the one to keep; the tour is a catalogue with no step I could take tomorrow, which is why it is a maybe. Bare agent names such as ruv-sgit and deck appear before a reader of this section alone knows who they are; the cast bar helps.
